label: input f or j during the original phase (context-gated)
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (96% of activation mass); it is near-silent in the copy phase and weak at <DEL> (3.5% of mass). It is token-selective: input f (14.7x lift, 29% of mass) and j (6.1x, 28%) dominate, then i, s, b (about 2-3x), mostly on the first occurrence of the token (92% of mass). It is strongly context-gated, though: only about 14% of f inputs and 6% of j inputs are active, and I could not find a simple history rule that fixes this. Seen-x/1 or prev2 conditions raised dev F1 only to about 0.39 and cut mass recall. Magnitude: f at t=0 always fires, but with tiny activation (100% precision, under 1% of mass). The largest activations come on f/j around t=1-3 and at the last original positions of long sequences (t=7-8, L=9), and these often carry a weaker echo onto the following <DEL> step. It does not fire on c, z, n, a, or digits, or during the copy outputs. Dev: f/j in original phase gives P=0.18, R=0.64, mass recall 0.56. Adding i, s, b on first occurrence raises mass recall to 0.76 at P=0.10.
